rv.q: The North American tour production, which opened Wednesday at the Hollywood Pantages, is a folksy farcical riot, wholesome enough for widespread appeal but with just enough flamboyant oddity to tickle the funny bone of urban sophisticates.
This is a laugh-a-minute (perhaps every 30 seconds!) comedic extravaganza that will leave you hungry for more.

This wildly original musical is a golden ear of comedy, wrapped in clever writing, helmed by powerhouse vocals, and buttered with some of the funniest deadpanned quips by Peanut ( Mike Nappi ) and the other cast members you'll hear on stage this season.
Basically, this was delightful, corny fun (yeah, I had to) from beginning to end and should not be missed.
SHUCKED hits that rare, sweet spot: warm, funny and a little bit bawdy, with butter-smooth vocals and just the right pinch of saltiness.
What begins as a wink‑and‑nod celebration of pun‑loving humor quickly reveals itself as a genuinely heartfelt Broadway musical with a sweet love story, toe‑tapping songs, and a whole lot of heart.
But... it's good. It's VERY good. It's a show I went into cynical about, as neither a country fan nor a rural person, but which won me over completely by about ten minutes into Act 1.
When it’s this funny, with this much amazing talent on stage, just relax and enjoy the corny ride.
SHUCKED is smart, silly, and full of charm.
For audiences looking for a smart, funny, and feel-good night at the theatre, this production delivers plenty to enjoy.
What makes SHUCKED so irresistibly appealing even to the most cynical of theatregoers is its sly, self-aware humor wrapped around a sincere emotional core.
The singing, dancing, acting, comic timing and preposterous storytelling, all work well.
Overall, SHUCKED succeeds as a winking modern musical that dares to be utterly, unapologetically silly and stupid—without sacrificing heart and soul.
The comedy spans from racy to ridiculous, but even when it edges on forced, the performers are met with long laughs and audience delight.
For fans of dad jokes, the show will be the stalk of the town.
Puns are allegedly the lowest form of humor. True or not, they make “Shucked” a corny delight.
Drop everything and go see Shucked while you can.
“Shucked” is, simply put, arguably the funniest comedy I have ever seen in a theater.
Seriously, this is the funniest new musical to come around to the Bay Area in ages.
Not for one second did I ever think watching people wax idiotic about corn could be turned into such a great musical.
This is theatre at its finest. Sit back, relax, laugh, repeat.
All in all, Shucked is two-and-a-half hours of pure escapism, pure joy, with laughs galore, great songs, an excellent production and an outstanding cast.

Shucked is a real crackerjack, an unapologetically cornball entertainment with such relentless puns, wildly charismatic ensemble and infectious glee, you could easily fail to recognize the solid craft.
What a delight it is to share that the national tour of Shucked, now playing at the Forrest Theatre, is a near-perfect, two-hour balm during this turbulent spring.
I found the whole show a pleasant, hilarious surprise, especially the company bow.
Happily, this self-proclaimed corny musical topped all my expectations.
“Shucked” will take you on a hayride of emotions and is a great date night experience for both Broadway and country fans alike, but be aware.

The jokes, as well as the songs, carry the show into the realm of something special, and it does what so many shows do not do: It returns the word comedy to the honorific “Musical Comedy,” which has almost gotten lost in recent years.
A new musical with modern sensibilities that definitely isn’t afraid of taking itself too seriously, “Shucked” is an absolute delight.
It’s never been so fun to consume your vegetables.
Let the plot unfold on its own, safe in the knowledge that the show delivers a sweet, corny time.
Shucked is a side-splitting musical-comedy that goes down smooth as a shot of corn whiskey.

As someone who’s seen her fair share of Broadway productions, I can confidently say this corny (pun absolutely intended) musical is one of the freshest, funniest shows to hit the road in recent memory.
This show is bright, silly, and refreshingly unpretentious.
Let’s just say that Maizy gets her man, and we get a crazy-wonderful musical perfectly tuned to lift our spirits.
With its satisfying element, it was easy to get shucked up at this — sorry, y'all — a-maize-ing show.
For two and a half hours, it’ll make you laugh, maybe cry, definitely tap your toes.
“Shucked,” on a Boston stop through April 20 of its North American tour, made me laugh.
Overall, “Shucked” is light on its feet, surprisingly warm, and built for a live audience.
If you enjoy a good laugh or a few dozen of them along with a good story filled with song, dance and romance, then this one is for you.
It's been a while since I've enjoyed a touring Broadway musical this much.
This show’s apolitical, outrageously silly humor and the warmth of its open-hearted characters make “Shucked ” a balm for the soul in today’s deeply divided America.

Theater Review: SHUCKED (National Tour) by Lynne Weiss | April 11, 2025 in Boston , Theater , Tours IT DON'T GET MUCH CORNIER– AND THAT'S THE POINT In Shucked , the jokes fly fast as exploding kernels of popcorn in this Tony-award winning musical comedy—part Brigadoon , part Music Man , and wholly the old TV show Hee Haw (which I’ve never...

Shucked is a true ensemble piece, and the cast and musicians worked wonderfully together. Robert Horn’s book brings steady pacing with whiplash one-liners, mostly from Peanut (Mike Nappi) and his frequent deep thoughts.
Shucked is pure, unpretentious fun.
If you love rapid-fire, eye-rolling puns, Shucked will fill you to overflowing.
I honestly haven’t laughed out loud this much at a musical in a long time.

For more than two hours, it pelts you with piffle so egregious — not just puns but also dad jokes, double entendres and booby-trapped retorts — that, forced into submission, you eventually give in and succumb to gelastic seizures and uncontrollable belly laughs.
I'd recommend seeing the show. It's a lot of fun.
On balance, though, “Shucked” delivers the goods.
Puns aplenty come flying at you like popcorn kernels, and the maize malapropisms will have you all ears (clearly they’re much better at it than we are).
If you liked any of those shows, you’ll like SHUCKED.
"Shucked" made me laugh. A lot, and often in spite of better judgment at the most groan-worthy moments in this rapid-fire script of jokes, puns and double entendres.
Grand vocals, fun choreography, and some slapstick round out a fun night of light entertainment with the promise of a neat and happy (and somewhat sappy) resolution by the end of act two.
It’s devilishly clever and stupendously dumb, in the best possible sense.
You won’t like “Shucked” if you can’t get a little corny with it.
Matched up to Brandy Clark and Shane McAnally’s somewhat simplistic but highly listenable country-pop score, “Shucked” weds sly intelligence to its overall good-natured down-homeness.
Because the comedy is bad-joke-driven the humor might seem simple. Not true. It's demanding, and thankfully everyone in the splendid cast has the gift of great comic timing.
"Shucked" offers the Broadway equivalent of a solid popcorn flick: an escapist romp through a maze of love, laughs and corn.
Laughter, no matter the reason, almost always gives the disheartened a ray of hope.
There’s a linguistic surprise—or two or three or four—on every page.

It has a few dry kernels and a predictable storyline, but with its pun-stuffed script, poppy hoedowns, and ridiculous devotion to the cob, it’s a fun one for anyone who loves a good groan-inducing dad joke — and it’s a sweet reminder to resist that fool’s gold out yonder and remember what’s beautiful in your own backyard.

Palm | mpalm@orlandosentinel.com | Orlando Sentinel PUBLISHED: June 25, 2025 at 5:00 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Corny musical about corn has lost some of its pop since its Broadway debut, but the touring version still lands its laughs.
"Shucked" is a sharply funny satire packed with innuendo and lightning-fast one-liners.
It asks nothing more from its audience than to sit back and enjoy. And isn't that enough?
Come for the music, stay for the puns and pick up a harmless souvenir or two at “Shucked.”

“Shucked” is a popcorn musical: lively, clunky, handsomely presented, good-natured, emotionally uninvolving, well-performed, overlong, heavily larded with jokes about penises and butts, occasionally quite witty yet frequently repeating aged gags from vaudeville and stand-up comedy.
But it fails as a sustained piece of musical theater, and that tacked-on happy ending is literally like watching corn grow.
But that style of Americana vaudeville depends on a certain tone and timing, which this show only intermittently achieved for me during its two-and-a-half-hour run.

cn.t: Critics find this pun-packed musical comedy relentlessly corny in the best way, with rapid-fire jokes and country charm earning consistent laughs despite predictable plotting and occasional groan-worthy humor.

vr.q: Oh, my gosh, what a treat.
